acceptance: A schema represents score type, methodology version, capability profile, S/M/L dataset vector, score-specific members, blocks, effective leaf/lineage weights, oracles, and reference vector.
Evidence status is enumerated as passed, failed_correctness, skipped_unsupported, skipped_infrastructure, timed_out, cancelled, or translation_failed; only passed is scoreable.

The result identity binds BenchBox revision; platform, adapter, driver, renderer and generator versions; post-translation SQL and parameters; source objects, rows and dataset hashes; hardware, OS, topology, tuning, cache, warmup, repetition, result-consumption, and timing-source policy.

Client-link identity includes cloud/region and the statement-overhead probe; tuning identity attests to indexes, materialized structures, caches, or settings created specifically for the scored manifest.
Throughput identity includes concurrency, session schedule, active interval, per-session configuration, and client/platform resource-accounting topology.
Fixture hashes and non-vacuity proof identities are required for admitted advanced leaves.
Canonical serialization and content hashes make manifests replayable and tamper-evident; compatibility tests reject undeclared or non-comparable changes.
context: Implements the proposed cross-benchmark score architecture. Preserve official TPC metrics as separate outputs. Numerical weights, size vectors, concurrency points, thresholds, and the M4 reference remain pilot hypotheses until methodology freeze.
description: Define versioned score-methodology, score-specific member, dataset-profile, schedule, qualification, and result-evidence schemas after oracle and non-vacuity contracts exist. Cohort identity binds software, hardware, deployment, data, translated SQL, tuning, locality, cache, timing, repetition, and concurrency state.
